_doc: BBB dating cabinet (#12, built 2026-07-16). THE OLDEST ENGLISH PIPE TRADEMARK (rhombus BBB = UK trade mark No. 39, filed 1876-01-01 -- the first pipe mark ever registered). Dates by: stem-logo generation (metal diamond rondel vs post-Cadogan stamped logo -- the GBD rondelle pattern again), line/patent years (Glokar 1905, Guardsman 1962), and hallmarked silver mounts (generic.json Birmingham/London charts -- BBB mounted heavily in silver). A 1960 BBB Catalog PDF exists (DiCuccio, linked on pipedia) -> FARID-FETCH.

history_anchors._doc: 1847 Adolph Frankau founds A. Frankau & Co, London (meerschaum importer); dies 1856; LOUIS BLUMFELD (18, on Thomas Carlyle's advice!) takes over -> BBB = Blumfeld's Best Briars, later understood as Britain's Best Briars. 1876-01-01: rhombus BBB = UK trademark No. 39 (+ No. 40 'B'). Own London factory at Homerton from 1898 (before that, low lines imported from Saint-Claude). 1920s: absorbed into A. Oppenheimer & Co; Cadogan Investments formed (this article says the Thirties, the GBD article says early 1920s -- sources disagree, noted). Homerton ran under Marechal Ruchon & Co (renamed Fairfax Traders in the 1970s) until Cadogan consolidated manufacture at SOUTHEND-ON-SEA after buying Orlik in 1980. Strong markets: British Empire + DENMARK (the most popular foreign brand there). Sub-brands/2nd marks (own rules): Capt. Kidd, Fairway ('F' in white), Frankau's, Glokar, Major Daff, Snap-Fit, Ultonia, Last Word, Mackenzie (filter brand, possibly Irish-made). Dunhill link: BBB turned Dunhill's Bent Magnum bowls until ~1923 (Esserman).

brand_marks.physical: Earlier pipes: METAL diamond/rhombus rondel with BBB embedded in the stem top; post-Cadogan-consolidation: STAMPED-ON logo (same evolution as GBD's rondelle). Heavy silver mounting tradition (hallmarked examples 1882-1920 documented) -> generic.json hallmark charts date them EXACTLY. Thirties: top lines got metal BBB inlay, bottom lines engraved only.

table.note: trademark floor 1876; own London production from 1898 (earlier + low lines = Saint-Claude imports)

line_years._notes: glokar: patent 1905 (hallmarked 1905 example = 'first year of the Glokar Patent'), BBB's Peterson-system answer, examples through 1913 -> end approx 1935 flagged. mackenzie: paper-filter brand pre-1900 (1891 Morell Mackenzie letter) -> 'survived until the Sixties'. carlton: metal-system pipe, retail 8/6 in 1938 -> floor 1938, end approx. rare grain/virgin/walnut/thorneycroft: the stable mid-1950s-60s Own Make lines -> [1950,1975] approx ('virgin'/'walnut' NOT encoded as keys -- collide with Comoy's Virgin Briar + generic finish words; confirm-flow). guardsman: UK PAT 35054/62 (filed 1962-09-14) -> floor 1962. best make: replaced Own Make at top in the Thirties AND survives as a Cadogan grade -> floor. own make: existed by ~1900 (1910 pricing documented), floor 1890 approx. two star (**) = Thirties bottom range, end approx. NOT encoded: Chubby/Golfer/Dreadnought/Bellerophon/Cutty (pre-1914 specials, no solid brackets -- Dreadnought suggests 1906+ but NOT sourced), Highland/Lovat sizes (Lovat = BBB-coined shape name, pre-1914), Ultonia Thule, Blue Peter (= Ultonia, not BBB-stamped), Super Stopping.

table.label: metal diamond BBB rondel in stem = pre-Cadogan-consolidation (ended when manufacture moved to Southend after 1980 -- approx, mirrors the GBD rondelle rule)
stamped-on BBB logo = post-Cadogan consolidation (like late GBD)

B.B.B. L.H.E. The above briars kept in stock, all from the best French makers' — B.B.B. pipes IN UK COMMERCE 3 years BEFORE the 1876 Trade Mark No. 40 registration, and explicitly FRENCH-MADE (pre-London-production era corroborated). Brand-predates-registration pattern (same as Civic 1919 vs 1921). The 1876 floors in this cabinet are TRADEMARK floors and stay; a BBB pipe cannot predate the brand's commerce (~1873 earliest print). 'L.H.E.' = third briar mark in the ad, unidentified — lead. (2) ★ 1881-06-29 Leeds Mercury p.1: four-ad slogan run each tagged 'BBB': 'BEST BRIAR PIPES always bear Trade Mark. Inquire of your Tobacconist — three B's in a diamond' + 'BRIAR ROOT PIPES are the BEST PIPES' + 'Warranted not to crack or burn' — the DIAMOND trademark described in print 1881 (earliest description we hold).
